newsitem.title: USA: Colombia's pipeline blast delays crude a few days.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's pipeline blast delays crude a few days.

text.p: Colombia's state oil company Ecopetrol has informed some customers that Cano Limon crude exports for October will be delayed a few days due to recent sabotage of its pipelines, traders said Thursday.
"Our October cargo was moved forward two days," a trader in South America told Reuters, but noted it was not a major delay and that he did not expect force majeure to be declared.
A U.S. Cano Limon customer added, "There's been nothing definitive, (delays) would not be more than a day or so."
Ecopetrol usually manages to avoid declaring force majeure by drawing stocks from storage when its pipelines have been sabotaged, traders said.
The company also makes adjustments to loading dates, which normally only delays shipments a few days.
Rebels attacked a key oil pipeline in northeast Colombia with a capacity of 220,000 barrels per day (bpd) on Tuesday, shutting it down for the second time in less than a week.
The line carries oil from the Cano Limon field operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp to the Caribbean port of Covenas. The pipeline has been dynamited 37 times this year.
But in spite of repeated sabotage, Ecopetrol's exports of crude oil to the U.S., around 250,000 bpd, are steadily on the rise due to the country's expanding production.
And frequent sabotage by guerillas and protesting farmers have not hindered crude sales within the region.
"The Colombian's are the world's experts on repairing pipelines. They seem to be able to handle it with minimal prolems," a U.S. crude trader said.
Last month, sabotage to the Trans-Andean pipeline suspended flows for 10 days, shutting in production by 60,000 to 70,000 bpd.
